yarn-troppo.meaning: Every beat survives, from the apprentices to "his head in the ash-barrel", and the asides hang off the original ("Counted 'em.", "Covers the lot, doesn't it?"). "patient, easygoing types" softens "forbearing", and "how dazzlingly you can't pick it" bends the uncertainty line.
yarn-troppo.sense: "can't pick it", "won't cop", "blow-ins" and "pollie" all fit. "chuffed with himself" is a British term rather than an Aussie one, and "easygoing" is not quite "forbearing".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much of it sounds like a local telling it: "out the back of the weather-clerk's factory", "The whole box and dice", "knock off a fair few poets". Some stock touches: "fair dinkum, he's earned every bit", "Crikey, what awful thunder", and British "chuffed".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than a level 2: a yarn opener "Here's one for ya.", tags like "the cheeky beggar", "scratches his noggin", "crisp as, cocky as you like" and added asides push it to a 3 or 4. No swearing, which fits vulgarity 0.
yarn-troppo.tone: The deadpan mostly survives, but the winks ("Should've kept it to themselves, ay?", "Hedging his bets, the cheeky beggar.") nudge Twain's dry irony into matey ribbing.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well, with short punchy sentences ("Weather to sell. To put in the bank."), but "how dazzlingly you can't pick it" is a clunky join.
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide spread with nothing leaned on: "mob", "learning the ropes", "box and dice", "blow-ins", "noggin", "brolly", "pollie".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the weather speech, but the added commentary ("Covers the lot, doesn't it?") explains jokes the original leaves to land on their own.

engine.meaning: The original almost word for word: "I reverently believe that the Maker who made us all makes everything in New England but the weather."
engine.sense: The few swaps fit: "a pollie had been there" for Congressman, "heaps of it" for plenty, "that bloke".
engine.authenticity: What little Aussie there is sits oddly in Twain's 19th-century prose: "that bloke that had that marvellous collection" and "heaps of it—a perfect grand review" are jarring joins rather than natural speech.
engine.register: Largely untranslated: apart from "bloke", "favourable", "heaps" and "pollie" it is the original, well under a level 2 light touch.
engine.tone: The tone is Twain's own, kept whole: "These are great disappointments; but they can't be helped."
engine.flow: Reads as the original does, with only small bumps where a slang word drops in: "there is going to be heaps of it—a perfect grand review".
engine.variety: Only a handful of terms, none repeated ("bloke", "heaps", "pollie"); nothing leaned on, but too little to show range.
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, nearly untouched: "you'll find that stranger down in the cellar with his head in the ash-barrel."

unharnessed.meaning: Every point is there, but the quoted forecast is reworded ("shifting to the southward", "likely patches of rain", "followed or preceded by earthquakes") when the original is a quotation, and "muck about" for "experiment" shifts the sense a little.
unharnessed.sense: "knock off a lot of poets", "blow-ins", "hasn't got a clue" fit. "muck about and learn the trade" strains: mucking about is idle fooling, not experimenting.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural ("chucked away everything with any sort of blemish", "a funny one"), but "I reverently reckon" is a forced collocation and "Strewth" in the stranger's mouth is a stock touch.
unharnessed.register: A light, even touch across the text: "reckon", "bloke", "blow-ins", "decent product". About level 2, no swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the deadpan: "These are big letdowns; but they can't be helped."
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly, apart from the clash in the opener "I reverently reckon" and "reckon" twice in two sentences.
unharnessed.variety: "reckon" twice up front, otherwise varied: "flabbergasted", "chucked away", "knock off", "blow-ins".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original, retold lightly; keeps "a Congressman had been through" and the full shape.

dinkum-3.meaning: Every point survives, including "weather to bank, weather to invest, weather to give to the poor" and the postscript; "mate" in the quote is colour.
dinkum-3.sense: "knocked the foreigners for six", "bumped up", "blow-ins", "a pollie had been through" all fit their contexts.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian telling it: "chucked everything with the slightest blemish", "a fair few poets", "proud as punch with his powers". "Strewth" is a little stock but sits in a quoted exclamation.
dinkum-3.register: A touch over level 2 with the opener "Here's one for ya." and "Don't you do it, mate", but otherwise a light hand. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the dry deadpan without winking: "These are big letdowns, but there's nothing you can do about them."
dinkum-3.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "So he came, and he made his whole collection in four days."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "bumped up", "knocked the foreigners for six", "brolly", "Yep", "pollie"; "Strewth" and "Here's one for ya." are stock tics.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the speech, shape and jokes intact, down to "his head in the ash-barrel".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point survives, from "raw apprentices in the weather-clerk's factory" to "a pollie had been there".
yarn-dinkum.sense: "won't cop", "blow-ins", "knocked the foreigners flat", "brolly" fit their contexts.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Mostly natural ("a fair few poets", "a funny one"), but the opener "Now, ya might've heard this one." is bolted on and "Crikey, what awful thunder" is stock.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, steady touch: "reckon", "Dunno", "blow-ins", "brolly". About level 2, no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the deadpan: "These are big letdowns, but there's no helping them."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth overall, but "reckon" comes twice in the first lines ("I reckon, hand on heart" and "but I reckon it must be").
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the original, retold lightly with its shape kept: "weather to give to the poor".

summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and mostly natural, but heavier than the level 2 brief and given to asides that explain Twain's jokes.
summaries.engine: Faithful because it is nearly the original; a few word swaps, far too light for the brief.
summaries.unharnessed: A light, faithful retelling at the right weight; a couple of forced swaps.
summaries.dinkum-3: Natural, faithful and smooth; the best balance of Aussie colour and Twain's deadpan.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Light, faithful and at the brief's weight; a stock opener and a repeated reckon.
